reader_summary: This is Pico's 1498 collected works, including the Life, the Apologia and the Oration. On two of four pages the transcription failed outright (model reasoning on one, a string of macrons on the other) and the English was supplied without a source: one is an invented summary, the other a different passage of the Oration. A third page is cut to a quarter. Where the transcription is complete (p. 18) both panes are careful and accurate, but a reader cannot tell which pages are real.
book_verdict: Two of four pages show English that does not translate the page (one invented, one a substituted passage of the Oration) and a third is truncated; the good page is good. Not fit to show until the failed OCR pages are found and redone.

reader_summary: This is Pico's short exposition of the Lord's Prayer (1537 printing), a devotional work rather than a Kabbalistic one. Transcription is of the right text and mostly exact; one page, made by a lighter engine, garbles several abbreviations. The English is faithful, with one small slip of sense and one sentence completed from beyond the page.
book_verdict: Sound reading text; a minor engine-mix page with garbled abbreviations and a completed last sentence. Show with the caveat that it is devotional, not Kabbalah.

title: Artis cabalisticae. Tomus I
shelf_note: Pistorius's 1587 anthology is the central printed corpus of Christian Kabbalah; the pages drawn are Ricius's De coelesti agricultura, Leone Ebreo's Dialogi, and Reuchlin's De arte cabalistica and De verbo mirifico.
structure_note: 1,136 page records against pages_count 1,120 and pages_translated field 1,114 (records report 1,136 translated): the counter fields are stale by 16–22. printed_backsteps 72 and printed_repeats 116 are many for one continuous pagination; an anthology volume with separately paginated preliminaries and some misread numerals would make some of them, but the scale suggests the count partly reflects split/cropped records from spreads (three of four images are crops) — worth an audit, not a defect seen on these pages.

reader_summary: This is Pistorius's 1587 Artis cabalisticae, the standard anthology of Christian Kabbalah, and the pages drawn come from Ricius, Leone Ebreo and two works of Reuchlin. The transcriptions are of the right pages and nearly exact (one two-line eye-skip). The English is close and readable, with a few slips of sense and one invented heading.
book_verdict: The strongest book in this packet: correct leaves, near-exact transcription, faithful English. Counter fields are stale and the backstep count deserves an audit.

title: [Vocabularius breviloquus]
shelf_note: The Vocabularius breviloquus (1478) is a general Latin dictionary attributed to Reuchlin; it has nothing to do with Kabbalah and sits on this shelf only by author.
structure_note: All four sampled pages carry the transcription (and translation) of the PRECEDING leaf: p.103 image begins 'in glo.l.i.ff.de iudi. Carduus...' while its OCR ends at 'Cardularij... sic tradit'; p.323 image is Nitrum–Nomen, OCR is Nicolaus–Nilus; p.381 image is Precator–Prefatus, OCR is Pragmatica–Prebenda; p.583 image is Maturo/'M ante E' Mechor–Mereo, OCR is Madeo–Manico. A consistent one-leaf text/image offset across the book, likely from the start. 668 records, 655 translated; the 54 printed numbers / 12 backsteps are leaf numbers and signatures in an unfoliated incunable and say nothing on their own.

reader_summary: This is the 1478 Vocabularius breviloquus, a Latin dictionary attributed to Reuchlin, not a Kabbalistic work. On every page sampled the transcription and English belong to the leaf before the one shown, so no page's text matches its image. The English may be a fair rendering of that wrong text, but a reader cannot use it.
book_verdict: A consistent one-leaf text/image offset on all four sampled pages, so the book needs realignment before anyone reads it; it is also on the wrong shelf for a Kabbalah reader.
